question_type: Midpoint ('Fisher Ideal symmetric') growth rate between two monthly yields from Table AY-1 (column 'Treasury bonds'), vintage pinned to FY1982-end issues; the answer is a unitless rate to 3 dp and the only knife-edge is output scale (bare fraction vs x100)
decisive_step: Output scale: '(in percent)' qualifies the input yields, the answer clause ('single numeric value rounded to three decimal places') names no percent, so the symmetric growth rate is committed as a decimal fraction, not multiplied by 100. Reference: worklog.md Step 8 and solution key_decisions ('I report a decimal fraction'; the percent form is listed as a rejected alternative). Table, column ('Treasury bonds 1/', not the neighbouring 'New Aa corporate bonds') and vintage (Sep/Oct/Nov 1982 issues all print the same two cells; 1983 issues redefine the series) were handled correctly by all three cells.

a.path_summary: Located AY-1 with find_tables (a[8]) and read the Aug rows of the Sep 1982 issue with show_table --grep Aug (a[19]), which printed both monthly Treasury-bond cells with their period labels. Its first calc (a[36]) wrote the midpoint formula as a bare ratio and never raised the percent question. It then chased the word 'new': printings (a[38]) surfaced a misparsed 'New Aa Treasury bonds 1/' weekly header in the Dec 1981 issue, and a fell into 22 identical 5-command cycles (a[40]-[250]: show_table 1982_09 --from-row 12 --grep Aug -> 'page rows 0-0', show_table 1981_12, two python raw reads, same THINK) until context compaction reset it at a[251]. After compaction it cited the AGENTS.md calc/provenance advice, re-ran printings (a[257]), show_table (a[259]) and calc with round(rate,3) (a[266]) and answered the printed fraction.

tool_use.friction: severe loop: 22 identical cycles a[40]-[250] (~15.7M input tokens, 738 s) ending only by compaction; show_table --from-row 12 --grep Aug returned 'page rows 0-0 of 12' every time (a[40], a[50], ... a[250]) - the row filter plus page offset yields nothing although rows exist; printings listed a 1981_12 weekly column misparsed as 'New Aa Treasury bonds 1/' (a[38]) which triggered the chase; a stray 'Treasury bonds' cell = 7 on a 1982_02 weekly row in the same printings output; sed without corpus path (a[21] exit 1)

The gate's `scale` rule flagged it as 100x the calc output with an offer of the bare fraction; b accepted without further reasoning (b[37]-[38]).

c.path_summary: Same table and cells as a: find_tables -> AY-1 (c[5]-[9]), show_table 1982_09 --grep Aug (c[12]) and a raw sed read (c[16]) gave both monthly Treasury-bond cells; printings confirmed them (c[21]) and c dismissed the misparsed weekly header (c[22]-[26]). smallest_change.change: Keep the submit-time `scale` check that saved b and extend it so it also fires when the x100 lives inside the calc expression: parse the source of the calc whose output the answer equals; if the expression contains a literal factor 100 or 200 (e.g. `200*(b-a)/(a+b)`, `(...)*100`) and the question's answer clause (the sentence containing 'report'/'answer'/'rounded') contains neither 'percent' nor '%', print: '[harness:gate] Your answer equals calc a949461e0090, whose expression multiplies by 100 (`200*(b-a)/(a+b)`); the question's answer clause does not ask for a percent. Offer: <the same value divided by 100, rounded as asked>'. b's trace shows the offer path works for this actor (accepted in one step, wrong-to-right).
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely - a and b's final answers were bare fractions so the rule stays silent; the risk is a question that wants a percent without saying so in its answer clause, which an offer (not a block) leaves to the model, and a's own 'Percent or fraction' text already states the same convention

alternatives.change: Make `calc` print a one-line scale note whenever its source contains a literal 100/200 factor: '⟦note⟧ expression multiplies by 100: this is a percent form; the bare fraction is <value/100>'. c would have seen the bare fraction printed at c[29] and had to choose between the two forms explicitly (its deliberation never contained the alternative).
alternatives.why_not_first: Weaker than the gate: it only surfaces the alternative, and the v8 prompt arm saw both forms and still chose x100 by prior; but it is cheap, runs where the decision is made, and needs no submit machinery.

alternatives.change: Rewrite a's 'Percent or fraction' bullet to name the trigger: 'A unit phrase on the inputs ("yield (in percent)") does not make a derived growth or change rate a percent; commit growth/change rates as decimal fractions unless the answer clause itself says percent or %.'
alternatives.why_not_first: c had the existing bullet and never invoked it; a was right without reading it; the v8 prompt arm had an even more specific lesson and still chose x100. Text is evidenced weak on this exact decision.

alternatives.change: Loop guard: after 3 identical commands with identical output, refuse the command and insert '[harness:loop] this command has printed the same output 3 times; decide with what you have or run something different'. a ran the same 5-command cycle 22 times (a[40]-[250]) until compaction; the AGENTS.md loop sentence did nothing.
alternatives.why_not_first: Cost only (a was right); it does not touch c's error.

fix.why_not_text: c ran with a's full AGENTS.md, including 'Percent or fraction: ... when it asks for a ratio, fraction or decimal, do not multiply by 100', and never cited it: its x100 framing was set in its first calc (c[29]) and its only deliberation was log vs midpoint (c[40]). a, with the same text, was right by an unexamined T=0 default (a[36]), not by the sentence. b's pre-gate reasoning (b[35]) and all three v8 arms chose x100 too. The decision is a strong actor prior triggered by the '(in percent)' token, and the only cell that flipped it was the one with a mechanical scale check (b).
fix.irreducible: partly: the formula name is non-standard and the percent-vs-fraction reading is a genuine ambiguity (the reference itself rated its confidence medium and its reviewer named scale as the residual risk); but the reference convention (answer clause silent -> fraction) is consistent and checkable

notes: Two tool defects visible here: (1) show_table `--from-row 12 --grep Aug` on the 1982_09 AY-1 returned 'page rows 0-0 of 12' although rows exist (a[40] and 21 repeats) - the offset plus row filter produce an empty page and gave a nothing to break its loop; (2) the 1981_12 AY-1 weekly panel header is parsed as 'New Aa Treasury bonds 1/' (a[38], b[28], c[21]) - a column-label misparse that matches the question's word 'new' and cost a ~200 steps and b/c a few steps each. printings also lists a stray 'Treasury bonds' weekly cell of a single digit on a 1982_02 row. The Oct 1982 printing carries a '5/' footnote prefix on the Aug 1982 cell, which printings reports as a 'REVISED/DIFFERS' text value (a[38], a[258]); a footnote-stripping parse would remove that false revision flag. For v10 controls: b is the clean demonstration that a deterministic scale check with an offer flips this actor wrong-to-right, and the pilot-1 analysis is right that the current rule would have missed c because c's x100 lived inside the calc expression; the rule should inspect calc source for literal 100/200 factors. The formula name is not in the corpus (a[34], b[34], c[27], c[35]); searching for it is wasted budget in every cell.
